description: Fixed safety information added to answers by NyayaAI's code (never written by the model). Every helpline was checked on an official government source on 2026-11-06. Shown when a VERIFIED citation comes from one of the listed Acts or sections, or (only when criminal law was searched) when the question contains one of 'show_for_keywords'.

helplines.text: In immediate danger, call 112 (national emergency number: police, fire, ambulance).
helplines.source: https://112.gov.in (Emergency Response Support System, Ministry of Home Affairs)

helplines.text: Women Helpline 181 (24x7) gives emergency and non-emergency support to women facing violence.
helplines.source: https://missionshakti.wcd.gov.in (Mission Shakti, Ministry of Women and Child Development)

helplines.text: Child Helpline 1098 (24x7) helps children in need of care and protection.
helplines.source: https://wcd.gov.in/child/child-helpline (Ministry of Women and Child Development)

helplines.text: For online fraud or cyber crime, call 1930 or report at https://cybercrime.gov.in as soon as possible.
helplines.source: https://cybercrime.gov.in (National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, Ministry of Home Affairs)

old_criminal_law.text: Your question mentions a date before 1 July 2024. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita came into force on 1 July 2024. For offences committed before that date, the old Indian Penal Code, 1860 may still apply, and cases already pending then continue under the old Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. NyayaAI does not contain the text of those old laws, so please check the old section numbers with a lawyer.
old_criminal_law.source: Commencement notifications dated 23 February 2024: S.O. 850(E) for the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and S.O. 848(E) for the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (footnotes to section 1 of each, India Code)
